 Ideastream Public Media's 2026 Election Guide 
 Ohio House - District 19
 Ed Hargate and Nicole Sigurdson are running for the Ohio House in District 19 on the Nov. 3, 2026 ballot. 
 Ohio House representatives create state laws, manage the state budget and help local residents connect with state government services. They serve two-year terms. 
 Ideastream Public Media contacted every candidate three times using contact information submitted to the Secretary of State's Office or on candidate websites and social media accounts to invite them to participate in our Voter Guide.
 Candidate responses have not been edited and are published as submitted.
 As necessary, our news team added contextual information clearly marked with an "editor's note" and in italics, though responses have not been uniformly fact-checked. With our small team, we are unable to proactively fact check every statement made by candidates, but will make every effort to make note of inaccuracies if they come to our attention.
 Please contact our news team at news@ideastream.org with questions or comments, or to report any errors.
 Ideastream Public Media's Voter Guide only includes candidates in contested races. 
 Ed Hargate
 Incumbent: No
 Party:  Republican
 Ideastream Public Media did not receive a response from this candidate.
 Nicole Sigurdson
 Lucas Sigurdson 
 Incumbent:  No
 Age on Election Day: 32
 Hometown: Cleveland
 Party: Democrat
 Why are you running for office? 
 I was raised with the simple but radical belief that we should care for one another. As a lifelong Ohioan, I know many of my friends and neighbors share that same value. We believe everyone deserves to feel safe, send their kids to great schools, build a secure career, and enjoy daily life in their community. However, extremists leading our state are making it harder to uphold these values. Wages aren’t keeping pace with the cost of living, housing prices are rising out of reach, and families are facing new environmental and economic challenges. Meanwhile, our conservative legislature is focused on stripping school funding, rolling back voting rights, restricting healthcare access, and targeting women and marginalized communities. I’m running because our district deserves a strong, dedicated voice in the Statehouse—someone who will fight for fair wages, fully fund our schools, and pass no-nonsense policies that strengthen families and communities.
 Through our " Listen Engage Vote " initiative, Ideastream asked voters to identify the issues they'd like to hear more about from candidates leading up to the election. The top three answers were education, data centers and the cost of living. What are your plans for those three issues, and what are your other top priorities? 
 On education, we have a responsibility to ensure every child in Ohio has access to a quality education by equitably and adequately funding our public schools. The Fair School Funding Plan enacted in 2021 is the closest we've come to doing that, and the state must pay its full share of the plan. Regarding data centers, we must limit their expansion in Ohio unless corporations are committed to paying the full cost of the operation including sales tax, powering the centers sustainably, and limiting the impact on our natural resources, including farmland. The cost of living must be addressed in myriad ways, but homeownership is a high priority. We must pass responsible property tax reform, providing necessary relief to vulnerable homeowners. We must expand opportunities for homeownership by increasing the housing stock and providing downpayment assistance. Further, we must increase access to affordable childcare, through initiatives such as the Childcare Tax Credit Act, and limit utility costs by investing in renewable energy development. Lastly and perhaps most importantly, we must ensure Ohioans are earning a living wage by increasing the minimum wage, requiring employers to have salary transparency, providing workforce development opportunities, and protecting collective bargaining rights. In addition to the important issues discussed here, I will work to protect our natural resources, especially Lake Erie, and advocate for the dignity of all, including our LGBTQ+ and immigrant populations.
 How do you plan to improve transparency and trust in government? 
 Building transparency and trust requires accessibility. As State Representative, my door will always be open and my office will prioritize constituent services. I plan to publish a monthly newsletter, to hold community office hours, and to attend community events as much as possible. In Northeast Ohio, we take pride in our communities, and I want to celebrate that pride through my service.
